sentences.text: Pirates kidnapped Julius Caesar and asked for twenty talents.
He was offended.
He told them to ask for fifty.
Around seventy-five B.C., young Caesar was sailing across the Aegean.
Cilician pirates grabbed him, and set his price.
Twenty talents?
For me?
Do you know who I am?
He sent his friends to raise the money, and stayed with the pirates for thirty-eight days.
When he wanted to sleep, he told them to be quiet.
He wrote poems, read them out loud, and called them illiterate barbarians if they didn't clap.
He joked he'd come back and punish them all.
They laughed.
The ransom arrived.
Fifty talents.
They let him go.
Caesar raised a fleet, without any official command.
He found the pirates on the same island, took back the silver, and captured them all.
And that joke about punishing them?
It wasn't a joke.
Never let your hostage negotiate his own price.
